analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The visible patch updates the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and extends the benchmark 'Runtime generation' row (head line 564) with `--runtime-concurrency <sizes>` and `--runtime-stagger`, citing RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark.swift. No executable code, config, or protocol changes are in the supplied evidence. The row states that benchmark runs keep the prefix cache off, which is consistent with T-041 (no new at-rest artifact and no change to the TTL or gating). Documentation touching other areas (logout/revocation at lines 501-550, switch, autopilot, cache) is unchanged context; it matches the stated threat-model scope for A-008/T-053 (bearer token sent only to the recorded issuer, only HTTP 204 confirms revocation) and TB-011 (no serving authorization from the OS choice). The file_changes head ranges list [1208,1209], but the supplied head text ends at line 828 (the unit was truncated), so I could not examine anything at 1208-1209 and that is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. The patch excerpt is also flagged incomplete. The new benchmark flags' implementation (RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark.swift) is not supplied, so any exposure from it (memory use, prompt-file handling, whether it writes output to disk) is unverified. Since this is documentation of a benchmark harness rather than serving, I see no concrete security regression. A deeper pass would need the text at 1208-1209 and the benchmark source.
